simple.meaning: אֵימָה (ʼêymâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “fright ; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

definitions.full: H367. emah אֵימָה 17 noun feminine terror, dread (Talmud id. , compare Assyrian imtu, Dl W ) — ׳א Gen 15:12 +; אֵימָ֫תָה Exod 15:16 (compare Ges § 90 , 2 R. b); construct אֵימַת Prov 20:2 ; suffix אֵימָתִי Exod 23:27 ; אֵמָתִי Job 33:7 , etc.; plural אֵימִים Jer 50:38 ; אֵמִים Job 20:25 ; אֵימוֺת Psa 55:5 ; suffix אֵמֶיךָ 88:16 ; — terror, dread (mostly in poetry), inspired by ׳י Exod 15:16 (song in E || מַּחַד ) 23:27 (E) Deut 32:25 ; Job 9:34 ; 13:21 ; compare 33:7 ; 20:25 ; Psa 88:16 (|| בִּעוּתִים חֲרוֺנִים, 88:17 ); compare Gen 15:2 גְדוֺלָה חֲשֵׁכָה אֵימָה ; occasioned by enemies Josh 2:9 ; Isa 33:18 ; Ezra 3:3 ; by king Prov 20:2 ; compare Psa 55:5 מָוֶת אֵימוֺת (|| מַּלָּצוּת רַעַד, יִרְאָה, 55:6 ); predicate of snorting of a war-horse Job 39:20 , of teeth of crocodile 41:6 ; plural figurative = idols (i.e. dreadful, shocking things) Jer 50:38 (|| מּסלים ).
definitions.rootNote: or (shortened) אֵמָה ; from the same as 366 ;

occurrences.englishText: When the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell on Abram. Now terror and great darkness fell on him.
Terror and dread falls on them.
I will send my terror before you, and will confuse all the people to whom you come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs to you.
She said to the men, “I know that Yahweh has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you.
In spite of their fear because of the peoples of the surrounding lands, they set the altar on its base; and they offered burnt offerings on it to Yahweh, even burnt offerings morning and evening.
Let him take his rod away from me.
withdraw your hand far from me,
He draws it out, and it comes out of his body.
Behold, my terror will not make you afraid,
Have you made him to leap as a locust?
Fearfulness and trembling have come on me.
Your fierce wrath has gone over me.
The terror of a king is like the roaring of a lion.
Your heart will meditate on the terror.
A drought is on her waters,
